description:
'''Funk carioca''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|ˈfɐ̃k(i) kɐɾiˈɔkɐ, - kaɾ-}}), also known as '''baile funk''', '''Brazilian funk''', or simply '''funk''', is a Brazilian [[hip hop music|hip hop]]-influenced [[music genre]] from [[Rio de Janeiro]], taking influences from musical styles such as [[Miami bass]] and [[Freestyle music|freestyle]].

In [[Brazil]], "baile funk" refers not to the music, but to the actual [[Dance party|parties]] or [[discotheque]]s in which the music is played ({{IPA|pt|ˈbajʎi}}, from ''baile'', meaning "[[Ball (dance event)|ball]]"). Although it originated in Rio ([[carioca]] is a Rio demonym), "funk carioca" has become increasingly popular among working classes in other parts of Brazil. In the whole country, funk carioca is most often simply known as "funk", although it is very different musically from the American genre of [[funk music]]. However, it still shows urban [[Afrobeat]] influences.
